# PocketPages

> PocketPages v1 is a file-routed, server-rendered page framework built into PocketOne (the `pages` extension): EJS, JSX or Markdown pages in pb_pages/, rendered inside PocketBase's JavaScript VM with a `ctx` API for requests, auth, data and assets.

PocketPages v1 runs in the `pocketone` binary, not Node; PocketPages 0.x (the npm package) is retired, see /docs/moving-from-0x. Agent Skill: https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/agent/skills/pocketpages (Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add pockethost/pocketone`).


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/moving-from-0x

# Moving from PocketPages 0.x

PocketPages v1 is part of PocketOne (the `pages` extension). It keeps the ideas of the npm package (a folder of files that become routes, EJS, layouts, middleware, private partials) and changes the shapes. Apps written for 0.x don't run unchanged.

There is no migration tool. Start a new app with `pocketone pages create <name>`, then move your pages over using the list below. The npm package is being retired.

## Folder and boot

| 0.x | v1 |
|---|---|
| `pb_hooks/pages/`, booted by `require('pocketpages')` in a `.pb.js` file | `pb_pages/` next to `pb_data`. No boot file, no npm install. |
| `create-pocketpages` | `pocketone pages create <name> [--starter <kit>]` |

Delete the `.pb.js` boot file and the `pocketpages` dependencies, and move the contents of `pb_hooks/pages/` to `pb_pages/`.

## The context object

0.x passed an `api` object and spread its members into each template. v1 passes one `ctx` object with `req`, `res`, `data`, `params`, `route` and helpers. See the [ctx reference](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx).

| 0.x | v1 |
|---|---|
| `request`, `response` | `ctx.req`, `ctx.res` |
| `body()`, `formData` | `ctx.req.body()` |
| `redirect(path)` | `ctx.res.redirect(path)` |
| `response.redirect(path, status)` | `ctx.res.redirect(path, status)` (unchanged) |
| `env()`, `store()`, `dbg()`, `info()`, `warn()`, `error()` | `ctx.env()`, `ctx.store()`, `ctx.log.debug()` / `info()` / `warn()` / `error()` |
| `auth`, `request.auth` | `ctx.auth` |
| `resolve(name)` | `ctx.resolve(name)` |

Inside templates, `data`, `params`, `asset` and `meta` are still available without the `ctx.` prefix. The other
0.x template globals are gone, including `resolve`, `redirect` and `env`: use `ctx.resolve()`, `ctx.res.redirect()` and
`ctx.env()`.

## Parameters, query strings and cookies

- Query parameters are no longer mixed into `params`, and nothing is JSON-parsed for you. `ctx.params` holds route parameters only; read the query string with `ctx.req.query(name)`, which returns strings.
- Cookies are strings. Pass `{ json: true }` to parse one: `ctx.req.cookie('prefs', { json: true })`.

## Middleware

0.x middleware either returned a value or called `next(extra)`, depending on how many arguments it declared. v1 has one signature:

```js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.data.user = ctx.auth
  return next()
}
```

Put shared data on `ctx.data`. See [Middleware](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/middleware).

## Loaders

`+load.js`, `+get.js`, `+post.js` and friends are replaced by one `+page.js` per folder that exports `load`, `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch` and `delete`. Returned objects are shallow-assigned into `ctx.data` (no deep merge). As in 0.x, every handler is optional and a page renders for any method, so templates that check the request method keep working (`request.method` becomes `ctx.req.method`).

```js
// 0.x: +load.js
module.exports = (api) => ({ products: $app.findAllRecords('products') })

// v1: +page.js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    return { products: ctx.app.findAllRecords('products') }
  },
}
```

See [Loading Data](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/loading-data).

## JSON

0.x sent template output as JSON if it parsed as JSON. v1 never does. Send JSON with `ctx.res.json()`, usually from a `+api.js` file. See [API Routes and JSON](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/api-routes).

## Layouts and slots

| 0.x | v1 |
|---|---|
| `<!-- slot:name -->` comments in the page | `slot('name', () => { %>...<% })` |
| `slot` and `slots.name` in layouts | `slot()` and `slot('name')` |

See [Layouts and Slots](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/layouts).

## Output

`echo()` is gone. A template returns its text; anything you want in the output goes through a tag. For streaming, use `ctx.res.sse()`.

## Flash messages

0.x put the message in a `?__flash=` query parameter with `redirect(path, { message })`. v1 uses a one-time cookie:

```js
return ctx.res.redirect('/account', { flash: 'Saved' })
```

Read it on the next request with `ctx.flash()`. See [flash](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/flash).

## Assets

`asset()` URLs now carry the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256, not the full hash.

## Configuration and plugins

- `+config.js` still takes plugin package names, which are loaded with `require` as before, but the packages must be
  v1 plugins: the 0.x `pocketpages-plugin-*` packages don't run on v1. `auth` and `realtime` are built in, EJS and
  Markdown are always on, and Datastar is an [add-on](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/datastar) you copy into `pb_pages/_private/` and list as `'datastar'`. Its API is 0.x's, with `signals()` added alongside `readSignals`. npm plugin package names and EJS options are gone.
- `+config.js` must export an object (`module.exports = { ... }`). 0.x's function form, `module.exports = (api) => ({ ... })`, is an error.
- A `package.json` at the app's root still works: bare `require('pkg')` looks in the app folder's `node_modules` after `pb_pages`.
- EJS and Markdown are always on. `pocketpages-plugin-ejs` and `pocketpages-plugin-marked` have no v1 equivalent because they aren't needed.
- The auth plugin no longer goes through the JS SDK over HTTP (`api.pb()`). Use `ctx.session.*`, which calls the app directly. See [Authentication](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/auth).

See [+config.js](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/config) and [Plugins](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins).

## Behavior that changed quietly

These don't fail with an error, so check for them when porting:

- **Cookies are `HttpOnly` by default.** Pass `{ httpOnly: false }` to `ctx.res.cookie` for a cookie your page's JS reads. The `pb_auth` cookie stays `HttpOnly`, so `pb.authStore.loadFromCookie(document.cookie)` in the browser no longer works.
- **Realtime messages are JSON-encoded.** `ctx.realtime.send(topic, data)` sends `JSON.stringify(data)`, so a string (such as an HTML fragment) arrives in quotes: `JSON.parse` it on the client. A `filter` now gets one argument, the client, and only narrows clients already subscribed to the topic.
- **`.md`, `.jsx` and `.tsx` files are always pages**, never served as static files.
- **Front matter is plain YAML.** EJS tags inside it aren't run.
- **`require` never leaves `pb_pages`.** To load code from `pb_hooks`, use `require(__hooks + '/lib/x')`.
- **Hook files (`*.pb.js`) go in `pb_hooks`.** In `pb_pages` they're an error and aren't served.

## Removed globals

| 0.x | v1 |
|---|---|
| `url()` | `ctx.req.url` |
| `stringify()` | `JSON.stringify` |
| micro-dash | plain JavaScript |
| `pb()` (JS SDK plugin) | `ctx.pb()`, built in: same SDK, no host setting, runs in-process as the signed-in user |

## Routing

A route with fewer segments no longer matches a longer URL. Segment counts must match: `products/[id].ejs` serves `/products/123` but not `/products/123/reviews`.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/agents

# Coding agents

Coding agents tend to write PocketPages as if it were a Node framework, or as if it were the 0.x npm package. The `pocketpages` Agent Skill teaches them v1: `pb_pages/`, `ctx`, routing, templates, layouts, auth and deploying. It's built from these docs and the v1 spec, so it changes when they change.

**Claude Code**

```
/plugin marketplace add pockethost/pocketone
/plugin install pocketone@pocketone
```

The plugin also has the `pocketone` skill, for the binary, `pocketone.yaml` and its extensions.

**Other agents that read Agent Skills** (Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and others)

```bash
npx skills add pockethost/pocketone
```

Or copy [`agent/skills/pocketpages`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/agent/skills/pocketpages) into your project.

# Installation

PocketPages v1 is built into PocketOne as the `pages` extension (`ext/pages`). There is nothing to install from npm: the standard `pocketone` binary includes it.

<%- include('quickstart') %>

`pocketone pages create myapp` creates a new app. Add `--starter <kit>` to start from a [starter kit](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/starter-kits).

_Note: `--dir` tells `pocketone` where `pb_data` is. PocketPages looks for `pb_pages` next to it. Create the superuser before the first `serve`; otherwise PocketBase opens its superuser installer in your browser._

Browse to `http://localhost:8090` and you'll see the starter's home page. The default `minimal` kit is one splash page:

<%- include('browser', { content: `<h1>PocketPages</h1>` }) %>

To start editing, open

```
myapp/pb_pages/index.ejs
```

Changes appear on the next refresh. The app doesn't restart.

## Where pages live

Pages live in their own folder next to PocketBase's others:

```
myapp/
  pb_data/  pb_hooks/  pb_migrations/  pb_public/
  pb_pages/
```

- PocketPages finds the folder at `pb_pages` next to `pb_data`, or wherever `--pagesDir` points.
- If the folder doesn't exist, the extension does nothing for that app.
- Under a multitenant host, every instance has its own `pb_pages`.

## How does it work?

PocketPages is a multi-page app server for PocketOne. It listens for requests and renders pages using file-based routing rules, like old-school PHP. URLs under `/api/` and `/_/` always belong to PocketBase. A URL nothing in `pb_pages` matches goes on to `pb_public`, then to PocketBase.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/starter-kits

# Starter Kits

To start a new app from a starter kit, run:

```bash
pocketone pages create myapp --starter <kit>
```

Without `--starter`, `pocketone pages create myapp` creates a plain app (the `minimal` kit). `pocketone pages starters`
lists the kits. The folder must not exist yet. Then run it:

```bash
cd myapp
pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data
```

`pocketone` keeps `pb_data` next to its executable unless you pass `--dir`; `pb_pages` and `pb_migrations` are found next
to `pb_data`.

Each starter kit is an ordinary `pb_pages` folder written against the v1 API, so everything in these docs applies to it.

| Starter | What it shows | Live demo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **minimal** | A minimal PocketPages starter with just the basics | [pocketpages-minimal.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-minimal.pockethost.io) |
| **mvp** | MVP.css, a minimalist classless CSS framework | [pocketpages-mvp.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-mvp.pockethost.io) |
| **auth** | Password, anonymous, OTP and OAuth2 sign-in, plus verification, password reset and email change | [pocketpages-auth.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-auth.pockethost.io) |
| **daisyui** | Tailwind CSS with DaisyUI components | [pocketpages-daisyui.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-daisyui.pockethost.io) |
| **daisyui-docs** | Documentation site template with DaisyUI and navigation | [pocketpages-daisyui-docs.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-daisyui-docs.pockethost.io) |
| **htmx** | HTMX integration for dynamic interactions | [pocketpages-htmx.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-htmx.pockethost.io) |
| **datastar** | Realtime chat and counter using Datastar | [pocketpages-datastar.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-datastar.pockethost.io) |


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/creating-a-page

# Creating a PocketPages Page

A **page** is a template file, `.ejs` or `.md`, anywhere in `pb_pages/`. Its path becomes its URL.

## Creating pages

1. **Create a file**: inside `pb_pages/`, create an `.ejs` file. For example, an "About" page:

```text
pb_pages/about.ejs  -> serves "/about"
```

2. **`index` files**: `index` maps to its folder.

```text
pb_pages/index.ejs           -> serves "/"
pb_pages/products/index.ejs  -> serves "/products" (and "/products/")
```

3. **Nested pages**: folders become URL segments.

```text
pb_pages/
├── index.ejs         -> "/"
├── about.ejs         -> "/about"
├── contact.ejs       -> "/contact"
└── products/
    ├── index.ejs     -> "/products"
    └── details.ejs   -> "/products/details"
```

4. **Markdown pages**: a `.md` file works the same way. It runs through EJS first, then Markdown. See [Markdown](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/markdown).

```text
pb_pages/docs/routing.md  -> "/docs/routing"
```

The extension is always dropped from the URL. To add data or handle forms, put a `+page.js` next to the page; see [Loading Data](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/loading-data).


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/directory-structure

# Directory Structure

All pages live in the `pb_pages/` folder, next to `pb_data/`:

```
myapp/
  pb_data/
  pb_hooks/
  pb_migrations/
  pb_public/
  pb_pages/
    +config.js
    +layout.ejs
    index.ejs
    about.ejs
    _private/
      nav.ejs
    assets/
      app.css
    products/
      [id]/
        +page.js
        index.ejs
```

## Special names

A file or folder name starting with one of these characters is never a URL:

| Prefix | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `+` | Framework file: `+layout.ejs` (or `.jsx`, `.tsx`), `+middleware.js`, `+page.js`, `+api.js`, one of each per folder. `+config.js`, `+error.ejs` and `+404.ejs` are allowed only at the top of `pb_pages`. Any other `+` name, any other extension (such as `+layout.md`), and a top-only file in a subfolder are errors at startup. |
| `_` | Private. `_private/` folders hold partials and modules for `include()` and `ctx.resolve()`. Other `_` names are ignored. |
| `-` | Ignored (drafts, notes). |
| `.` | Ignored (dotfiles), except a top-level `.well-known/`, which is served as static files (ACME challenges, `security.txt`, app links). |

`node_modules/` is never routed either.

## Groups

A folder named `(name)` groups files without adding a URL segment: `(marketing)/pricing.ejs` serves `/pricing`. A group can have its own `+layout.ejs`, `+middleware.js` and `_private/`.

## What else

- Every other file is a [static file](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/static-content), served as-is.
- Page code can `require()` modules by name from `_private/` folders (nearest first), then `pb_pages/node_modules`, then
  `pb_hooks/node_modules` and the app folder's `node_modules`, then the app's usual module paths.
- Pages' own file access (routes, static files, includes, assets) never leaves `pb_pages`.
- A `pb_pages/api/` folder is an error at startup, because `/api/` belongs to PocketBase.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/routing

# File-Based Routing

URLs come from the files and folders in `pb_pages/`.

## Pages

| File | URL |
|---|---|
| `index.ejs` | `/` |
| `about.ejs` | `/about` |
| `docs/index.md` | `/docs` (and `/docs/`) |
| `docs/routing.md` | `/docs/routing` |
| `products/[id].ejs` | `/products/123`, with `ctx.params.id = "123"` |
| `[org]/[repo]/index.ejs` | `/acme/web`, with `ctx.params = { org: "acme", repo: "web" }` |

- The extension is dropped. `index` maps to its folder.
- `[name]` matches exactly one non-empty segment. A parameter must be the whole segment: `post-[id].ejs` is an error at startup.
- Segment counts must match: `products/[id].ejs` doesn't match `/products/123/reviews`.
- A URL with a trailing slash matches the same route as without it. Pages never redirect to add or remove one.
- Matching is case-sensitive.

See [Accessing Parameters](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/parameters).

## Groups

A folder named `(name)` doesn't add a URL segment. Use groups to give part of the site its own layout or middleware:

```text
pb_pages/
  (site)/
    +layout.ejs     # wraps everything in (site)
    index.ejs       # /
    about.ejs       # /about
  xapi/
    count.ejs       # /xapi/count, outside the (site) layout
```

## API routes

A `+api.js` file serves its folder's URL without a template: `feeds/rss/+api.js` serves `/feeds/rss`. `[param]` folders work as for pages. A folder can't have both a `+api.js` and an `index` page. See [API Routes and JSON](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/api-routes).

A `+page.js` in a folder with no page serves the folder's URL from JS too: `logout/+page.js` serves `/logout`. See [Pages without a template](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/loading-data#pages-without-a-template).

## Static files

Every other file is served as-is at its path, with groups removed: `assets/app.css` serves `/assets/app.css`. See [Static content](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/static-content).

## Which route wins

1. `/api/...` and `/_/...` belong to PocketBase. Pages never see them.
2. Among matching routes the most specific wins: segments are compared from the left, and a literal segment beats a `[param]`. So `products/new.ejs` beats `products/[id].ejs` for `/products/new`.
3. A static file and a page can't claim the same URL (startup error).
4. A URL nothing in `pb_pages` matches goes on to `pb_public`, then to PocketBase.

## When routes change

The route table is built when the app starts and rebuilt whenever anything in `pb_pages` changes. A rebuild never restarts the app or reloads `pb_hooks`. Startup errors (bad names, conflicts) are logged with the file path, and the previous route table keeps serving.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/parameters

# Route and Query Parameters

Route parameters come from the URL path. Query parameters come from the query string. v1 keeps them apart.

## Route parameters

Use square brackets in file or folder names to capture a URL segment:

```
pb_pages/
  products/
    [productId]/
      index.ejs
      reviews/
        [reviewId].ejs
```

This handles URLs like `/products/123` and `/products/123/reviews/456`.

Read them through `params` (the same object as `ctx.params`):

```ejs
<!-- products/[productId]/reviews/[reviewId].ejs -->
<h1>Product: <%= params.productId %></h1>
<p>Review: <%= params.reviewId %></p>
```

Route parameters are always strings. `ctx.params` never includes query parameters.

## Query parameters

Read the query string with `ctx.req.query()`:

```
/products/123?sort=latest&tag=red&tag=blue
```

```ejs
<p>Sort by: <%= ctx.req.query('sort') %></p>
<p>Tags: <%= ctx.req.query('tag', { all: true }).join(', ') %></p>
```

| Call | Returns |
|---|---|
| `ctx.req.query(name)` | First value as a string, or `undefined` |
| `ctx.req.query(name, { all: true })` | Every value, as an array of strings |
| `ctx.req.query()` | `{ name: firstValue }` for every parameter |

Values are strings. Nothing is parsed for you; if you pass JSON in a query parameter, parse it yourself:

```js
const filters = JSON.parse(ctx.req.query('filters') ?? '{}')
```

## The route itself

`ctx.route` describes the matched route: `{ path, name, file }`. For `products/[productId]/index.ejs`, `path` is `/products/[productId]`, `name` is `index`, and `file` is `products/[productId]/index.ejs`.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/loading-data

# Loading Data in PocketPages

You can load data right in a template, or in a `+page.js` file next to it.

## Inline data loading

The simplest way is a `<% %>` block at the top of your template:

```ejs
<%
  const products = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'active = true', 'name', 100)
%>

<h1>Products</h1>
<% for (const product of products) { %>
  <div class="product">
    <h2><%= product.getString('name') %></h2>
  </div>
<% } %>
```

## Server script blocks

For better formatting support in editors, you can write `<script server<%- '>' %>` instead of `<% %>`. They mean the same thing:

```ejs
<script server<%- '>' %>
  const products = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'active = true', 'name', 100)
  const categories = ctx.app.findAllRecords('categories')
</script>

<h1>Products by Category</h1>
<% for (const category of categories) { %>
  <h2><%= category.getString('name') %></h2>
<% } %>
```

## Structured loading with `+page.js`

A `+page.js` file keeps data loading and form handling out of the template:

```js
// pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    ctx.data.product = ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id)
  },
  post(ctx) {
    const { qty } = ctx.req.body()
    // ...
    return ctx.res.redirect(`/products/${ctx.params.id}`, { flash: 'Added to cart' })
  },
}
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/products/[id]/index.ejs -->
<h1><%= data.product.getString('name') %></h1>
<% const flash = ctx.flash() %>
<% if (flash) { %><p><%= flash %></p><% } %>
```

### Exports

`+page.js` exports any of `load`, `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch` and `delete`.

1. `load` runs first, for every method.
2. Then the handler for the request method runs, if there is one.
3. Then the page renders.

A handler can set fields on `ctx.data`, or return a plain object. A returned object is shallow-assigned into `ctx.data` (`Object.assign`); there is no deep merge.

```js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    return { departments: ctx.app.findAllRecords('departments') }
  },
  get(ctx) {
    ctx.data.mode = 'view'
  },
}
```

If a handler sends a response (`ctx.res.redirect`, `json`, `html`, `text`, `file`, `sse`), the page doesn't render.

### One `+page.js` per folder

A `+page.js` applies to every page in its folder. Use `ctx.route.name` to tell them apart:

```js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    if (ctx.route.name === 'details') {
      ctx.data.reviews = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('reviews', 'product = {:id}', '-created', 20, 0, { id: ctx.params.id })
    }
  },
}
```

### Methods without a handler

Every handler is optional. A page renders for any method, like PHP, so a template can handle a form on its own:

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/contact.ejs, no +page.js -->
<% if (ctx.req.method === 'POST') { %>
  <p>Thanks, <%= ctx.req.body().name %>!</p>
<% } else { %>
  <form method="post"><input name="name" /><button>Send</button></form>
<% } %>
```

A `post` (or `put`, ...) handler in `+page.js` is the tidier place for form logic as a page grows, but you don't need
one. Only routes with nothing to render, [`+api.js`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/api-routes) and a `+page.js` without a page, answer `405`
for a method they have no handler for.

## Example: a contact form

```js
// pb_pages/contact/+page.js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    return { departments: ctx.app.findAllRecords('departments') }
  },
  post(ctx) {
    const { email, message, department } = ctx.req.body()
    try {
      const record = new Record(ctx.app.findCollectionByNameOrId('messages'))
      record.set('email', email)
      record.set('message', message)
      record.set('department', department)
      ctx.app.save(record)
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: 'Failed to send message', values: { email, message, department } }
    }
    return ctx.res.redirect('/contact', { flash: 'Thanks, we got your message.' })
  },
}
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/contact/index.ejs -->
<% const flash = ctx.flash() %>
<% if (flash) { %><p><%= flash %></p><% } %>
<% if (data.error) { %><mark><%= data.error %></mark><% } %>

<form method="post">
  <input name="email" type="email" value="<%= data.values?.email %>" />
  <select name="department">
    <% for (const d of data.departments) { %>
      <option value="<%= d.id %>"><%= d.getString('name') %></option>
    <% } %>
  </select>
  <textarea name="message"><%= data.values?.message %></textarea>
  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>
```

## Pages without a template

A `+page.js` in a folder with no page file serves the folder's URL from JS. Use it for a page you'd rather build in
code, or for a URL that only acts and redirects:

```js
// pb_pages/logout/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.signOut()
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

```js
// pb_pages/hello/+page.js
module.exports = {
  get(ctx) {
    return ctx.res.html(`<h1>Hello ${ctx.auth ? ctx.auth.getString('name') : 'there'}</h1>`)
  },
}
```

- With no template to render, each handler must send a response; returning without one is a 500.
- Methods without a handler answer `405`, `GET` included: `/logout` above only takes `POST`.
- Folder middleware runs; layouts don't, so wrap HTML yourself (or render a partial with `ctx.include`).
- Errors show your `+error.ejs` page. For JSON responses and JSON errors, use [`+api.js`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/api-routes) instead.

## Middleware or `+page.js`?

- Only the route's own folder's `+page.js` runs.
- Every `+middleware.js` from `pb_pages/` down to the route's folder runs, root first.

Use [middleware](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/middleware) for data or checks that a whole section of the site shares.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/api-routes

# API Routes and JSON

A `+api.js` file serves its folder's URL without a template. Use it for JSON, feeds, webhooks and anything else that isn't an HTML page.

```js
// pb_pages/feeds/latest/+api.js
module.exports = {
  get(ctx) {
    const posts = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('posts', 'published = true', '-created', 20)
    return ctx.res.json(posts.map((p) => ({ id: p.id, title: p.getString('title') })))
  },
}
```

A request to `/feeds/latest` returns:

```json
[{ "id": "abc123", "title": "Hello" }]
```

## How it works

- `+api.js` has the same exports as `+page.js`: `load`, `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`.
- There is no template, so a handler must send a response. Returning without one is a `500`.
- `[param]` folders work as for pages: `products/[id]/+api.js` serves `/products/123`.
- A folder can't have both a `+api.js` and an `index` page.
- Middleware runs for API routes too.
- `ctx.httpError()` thrown in a `+api.js` answers with JSON: `{ "status": 404, "message": "..." }`.

## Sending responses

| Call | Sends |
|---|---|
| `ctx.res.json(data)` / `ctx.res.json(status, data)` | JSON |
| `ctx.res.text(text)` / `ctx.res.text(status, text)` | Plain text |
| `ctx.res.html(html)` / `ctx.res.html(status, html)` | HTML as-is, without layouts |
| `ctx.res.file(path)` | A file from `pb_pages` |
| `ctx.res.redirect(location)` | A redirect |
| `ctx.res.sse()` | A `text/event-stream` |

See [res](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/res).

## JSON from a page

JSON is only sent through `ctx.res.json` (or a `+api.js`). Template output is never parsed as JSON, even if it looks like JSON. A page's `+page.js` can still answer with JSON for one method:

```js
// pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const product = ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id)
    return ctx.res.json({ id: product.id, name: product.getString('name') })
  },
}
```

## Keep `/api/` free

`/api/` belongs to PocketBase. Pages never see it, and a `pb_pages/api/` folder is an error at startup. Put your routes somewhere else, such as `feeds/`, `xapi/` or `hooks/`.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ejs

# EJS

EJS is always on. There is nothing to install or configure.

## Tags

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<% code %>` | Run JS, no output |
| `<%= expr %>` | Output, HTML-escaped |
| `<%- expr %>` | Output, raw |
| `<%# comment %>` | Nothing |
| `<%%` | A literal `<%` |
| `-%>` | Also remove the newline right after the tag |
| `<%_` / `_%>` | Also remove whitespace before / after the tag on its line |
| `<script server<%- '>' %> code </script>` | Same as `<% code %>` |

## Escaping

`<%= %>` replaces `&` `<` `>` `"` `'` with `&amp;` `&lt;` `&gt;` `&#34;` `&#39;`. `null` and `undefined` output as an empty string.

```ejs
<p><%= '<b>"x"</b>' %></p>   <!-- <p>&lt;b&gt;&#34;x&#34;&lt;/b&gt;</p> -->
<p><%- '<b>raw</b>' %></p>    <!-- <p><b>raw</b></p> -->
<p><%= null %></p>            <!-- <p></p> -->
```

Use `<%-` only for HTML you trust, such as the output of `include()` or `slot()`.

## In scope

Inside a template you can use:

| Name | |
|---|---|
| `ctx` | The [request context](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx) |
| `data` | `ctx.data` |
| `params` | `ctx.params` |
| `include` | Render a [partial](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/partials) |
| `slot` | Define or read a [slot](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/layouts) |
| `asset` | `ctx.asset` |
| `meta` | `ctx.meta` |
| `require` | Load a module: a path, or a name looked up in `_private/` then `node_modules` (see [JavaScript Runtime](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/jsvm)) |

## Output

A template returns its text. There is no `echo()`; anything you want in the output goes through a tag.

```ejs
<ul>
<% for (const n of [1, 2]) { -%>
  <li><%= n %></li>
<% } -%>
</ul>
```

## Caching

A template is compiled once per content hash and reused, so an edited file is recompiled on the next request.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/markdown

# Markdown Support

A `.md` file is a page, just like an `.ejs` file. Markdown is always on.

## How it works

1. **EJS first**: the file runs through EJS, so every [EJS tag](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ejs) works in Markdown.
2. **Then Markdown**: the result is rendered as Markdown: CommonMark plus GFM tables, strikethrough, task lists and autolinks.

## Front matter

YAML between `---` lines at the top of the file is front matter. Each top-level key is passed to `ctx.meta(key, value)`:

```markdown
---
title: My Blog Post
description: A detailed guide about something interesting
---

# Content starts here...
```

Read the values in a layout with `meta`:

```ejs
<title><%= meta('title') %></title>
<meta name="description" content="<%= meta('description') %>">
```

## Headings

Headings get `id`s, so you can link to them: the text is lowercased, characters other than `a-z`, `0-9`, `-`, `_` and space are removed, and spaces become `-`. `## Front matter` gets `id="front-matter"`.

## Images

Relative image paths go through [`ctx.asset`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/asset), so they get fingerprinted URLs:

```markdown
![Logo](logo.png)
```

## Markdown partials

A `.md` file in a `_private/` folder can be included from EJS with `include()`. It's rendered the same way, EJS then Markdown:

```ejs
<%- include('intro') %>
```

## Notes

- Layouts are `+layout.ejs`, `+layout.jsx` or `+layout.tsx`. A layout can't be Markdown: `+layout.md` is an error at
  startup. A Markdown page is still wrapped by the layouts above it.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/jsx

# JSX and TSX

A `.jsx` or `.tsx` file is a template, just like an `.ejs` file. It can be a page, a layout (`+layout.tsx`), an error page (`+error.tsx`, `+404.tsx`) or a partial in `_private/`. PocketOne compiles it the first time it's used, with esbuild built into the binary: no Node, no `npm install`, no build step. TypeScript types are stripped, not checked.

```tsx
// pb_pages/products/[id].tsx
import Price from './_private/Price'

export default function Product({ data, slot }: any) {
  slot('title', data.product.getString('name'))
  return (
    <article class="product">
      <h1>{data.product.getString('name')}</h1>
      <Price cents={data.product.getInt('price')} />
    </article>
  )
}
```

```tsx
// pb_pages/products/_private/Price.tsx
export default ({ cents }: { cents: number }) => <span class="price">${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)}</span>
```

## Props

The file's default export is a component: a function from props to markup. It gets:

| Prop | |
|---|---|
| `ctx` | The [request context](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx). |
| `data`, `params`, `meta` | The same as `ctx.data`, `ctx.params` and `ctx.meta`. |
| `asset`, `include` | The same helpers EJS templates have. `include(name, locals)` returns HTML you can put in JSX. |
| `slot` | `slot(name)` reads a named slot, `slot(name, content)` sets one, `slot()` is the inner content. |
| `children` | In a layout, the inner content. |

A partial also gets the locals it was included with, as props. EJS can include a `.jsx` or `.tsx` partial the same way: its locals become props.

## Server-rendered HTML only

JSX renders straight to HTML on the server. There's no virtual DOM, no hydration and no client-side React.

- Event handler props (functions) are dropped. Use plain attributes: `onclick="..."`, `hx-get`, `data-on:click`.
- Text and attribute values are escaped. `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }}` inserts raw HTML.
- `class` and `className` both work, as do `for` and `htmlFor`.
- `style` takes a string or an object: `{ marginTop: 4 }` renders `margin-top:4`.
- `true` renders a bare attribute. `false`, `null` and `undefined` leave it out.
- `<html>` gets `<!doctype html>` in front of it, since JSX can't write a doctype.

## Layouts

```tsx
// pb_pages/+layout.tsx
export default function Layout({ children, slot }: any) {
  return (
    <html>
      <head>
        <title>{slot('title')}</title>
      </head>
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

Layouts in `.ejs`, `.jsx` and `.tsx` mix freely: an EJS page can sit inside a TSX layout and the other way round.

## TypeScript modules

`+page.ts`, `+api.ts`, `+middleware.ts`, `+config.ts` and any `.ts` file reached by `require` or `import` work like their `.js` versions. A module whose only export is `export default` behaves like `module.exports = ...`.

Components are ordinary modules, so `import Card from './_private/Card'` resolves the same way as [`require`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/jsvm). When a partial name has no extension, `.ejs`, `.md`, `.jsx` and `.tsx` are tried, in that order.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/partials

# Using Partials in PocketPages

Partials are reusable templates that you include from other templates. They live in `_private/` folders, which are never routed.

## Including a partial

```ejs
<%- include('nav') %>
<%- include('card', { product }) %>
```

- `include(name, locals?)` renders a template from a `_private/` folder and returns its text. Use `<%-` so its HTML isn't escaped.
- `name` may omit the extension; `.ejs`, `.md`, `.jsx` and `.tsx` are tried, in that order.
- The partial sees the same `ctx`, plus `locals` as top-level variables.
- `locals` is also the whole object, as in EJS. Use it for optional values: `<%= title %>` throws if `title` wasn't passed, but `<% if (locals.subtitle) { %>` doesn't.
- Including more than 64 levels deep is an error.

## Where partials are found

```
pb_pages/
  _private/
    header.ejs
    footer.ejs
  blog/
    _private/
      sidebar.ejs
    posts/
      _private/
        post-card.ejs
      index.ejs
```

PocketPages looks in `_private/` in the current template's folder, then in each parent folder up to `pb_pages/`.

```ejs
<!-- In blog/posts/index.ejs -->
<%- include('post-card', { post }) %>  <!-- blog/posts/_private/post-card.ejs -->
<%- include('sidebar') %>              <!-- blog/_private/sidebar.ejs -->
<%- include('header') %>               <!-- _private/header.ejs -->
```

A name starting with `/` looks only in `pb_pages/_private/`:

```ejs
<%- include('/header') %>  <!-- always pb_pages/_private/header.ejs -->
<%- include('/blog/_private/sidebar') %>  <!-- a path that names a _private folder: blog/_private/sidebar.ejs -->
```

The extension is optional. A dotted name such as `include('nav.main')` finds `nav.main.ejs`.

This means you can:

- Keep section-specific partials in that section's `_private/`.
- Hoist a shared partial up to a common parent.
- Override a parent's partial with a local one of the same name, and still reach the root one with `/name`.

## Passing data

Pass only what the partial needs:

```ejs
<%- include('user-card', { name: user.getString('name'), joined: user.getString('created') }) %>
```

```ejs
<!-- _private/user-card.ejs -->
<div class="card">
  <h3><%= name %></h3>
  <p>Joined <%= joined %></p>
</div>
```

Partials can also read `ctx`, `data` and `params` directly. Passing values explicitly keeps them easy to reuse.

## Markdown partials

A `.md` partial is rendered as EJS, then Markdown:

```ejs
<%- include('intro') %>  <!-- _private/intro.md -->
```

## JavaScript modules

`_private/` folders also hold JS modules. Load them with [`ctx.resolve()`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/resolve), which uses the same lookup.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/layouts

# Layouts and Slots

`+layout.ejs` files wrap pages. A page's layouts are every `+layout` from its own folder up to `pb_pages/`, applied innermost first. A folder may have one layout, written as `+layout.ejs`, `+layout.jsx` or `+layout.tsx`. A layout can't be Markdown: `+layout.md` is an error at startup.

```plaintext
pb_pages/
  +layout.ejs          # applied last (outermost)
  products/
    +layout.ejs        # applied first
    [id].ejs
```

For `/products/123`, `[id].ejs` renders, then `products/+layout.ejs` wraps it, then `+layout.ejs` wraps that.

## `slot()`

In a layout, `slot()` returns the content being wrapped: the page, or the inner layout.

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/+layout.ejs -->
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <title>My Application</title>
</head>
<body>
  <main>
    <%- slot() %>
  </main>
  <footer>&copy; <%= new Date().getFullYear() %> My Application</footer>
</body>
</html>
```

`<%- slot %>` without parentheses prints the same content, so 0.x layouts that wrote it still work.

## Named slots

A page (or an inner layout) defines a named slot with `slot(name, fn)`. `fn`'s output is captured and nothing is output in place. A layout reads it with `slot(name)`, which returns `''` if it isn't defined.

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/products/[id].ejs -->
<% slot('title', () => { %><%= data.product.getString('name') %><% }) %>
<h1><%= data.product.getString('name') %></h1>
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/+layout.ejs -->
<html>
  <head><title><%- slot('title') || 'My shop' %></title></head>
  <body><%- slot() %></body>
</html>
```

- Named slots defined by the page or by any inner layout are visible to every outer layout.
- Defining the same name again replaces it. Inside the new definition's `fn`, `slot(name)` still returns the previous content, so a layout can wrap it:

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/docs/+layout.ejs -->
<% slot('title', () => { %>Docs: <%- slot('title') %><% }) %>
<main><%- slot() %></main>
```

## Data in layouts

Layouts render after the page, with the same `ctx`. Everything middleware, `+page.js` and the page put on `ctx.data` or `ctx.meta` is there.

## When layouts are skipped

- When the response isn't HTML (a handler set another `Content-Type`).
- When a handler or middleware sent the response itself (`ctx.res.json`, `ctx.res.html`, `ctx.res.redirect`, ...).
- For `+api.js` routes, which have no template.
- After `ctx.res.layout(false)`, called from middleware, `+page.js` or the page itself.
- With the [Datastar add-on](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/datastar), for requests that carry `Datastar-Request: true`.

To serve HTML fragments without the site layout, call `ctx.res.layout(false)`, put the layout in a group (`(site)/+layout.ejs`) and the fragments outside it, or send them with `ctx.res.html()`.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/private-files

# Working with Private Files and Directories

## Names that are never routed

| Prefix | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `+` | Framework file (`+layout.ejs`, `+page.js`, ...) |
| `_` | Private. `_private/` folders hold partials and modules. Other `_` names are ignored. |
| `-` | Ignored (drafts, notes) |
| `.` | Ignored (dotfiles) |

```
pb_pages/
  _private/        # private (not routable)
  -drafts/         # ignored
  helpers/         # normal folder (routable)
  +page.js         # framework file (not routable)
  +layout.ejs      # framework file (not routable)
  index.ejs        # page
```

## The `_private` folder

`_private/` folders serve two purposes:

1. Template partials, rendered with [`include()`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/partials)
2. JavaScript modules and other files, loaded with [`ctx.resolve()`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/resolve)

Both use the same lookup: `_private/` in the current template's folder, then each parent folder up to `pb_pages/`. A name starting with `/` looks only in `pb_pages/_private/`.

```
pb_pages/
  _private/
    header.ejs
    format.js
  products/
    _private/
      product-card.ejs
      queries.js
    index.ejs
```

```ejs
<!-- In products/index.ejs -->
<%
  const queries = ctx.resolve('queries')   // products/_private/queries.js
  const format = ctx.resolve('format')     // _private/format.js
%>
<%- include('header') %>                  <!-- _private/header.ejs -->
<% for (const p of queries.featured(ctx.app)) { %>
  <%- include('product-card', { p, format }) %>
<% } %>
```

## Modules

A module in `_private/` is a CommonJS file:

```js
// pb_pages/products/_private/queries.js
module.exports = {
  featured: (app) => app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'featured = true', '-created', 10),
}
```

## Notes

1. Files in `_private/` are never served.
2. Keep secrets in environment variables (see [Managing Secrets](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/secrets)), not in files.
3. Keep private files close to where they're used, and hoist them up when several sections share them.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/middleware

# Middleware

Middleware files (`+middleware.js`) run before your handlers and templates. Use them to:

- Check authentication
- Load data a whole section shares
- Set headers
- Validate requests

## Basic example

```js
// pb_pages/admin/+middleware.js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
  ctx.data.section = 'admin'
  return next()
}
```

- One signature: `(ctx, next)`. Call `next()` to continue, and return its result.
- Returning without calling `next()` ends the request. If no response was sent, that's an error (a `500`; in dev mode the error page names the middleware file).
- Share data through `ctx.data`.

## Order

Every `+middleware.js` from `pb_pages/` down to the route's folder runs, root first. Groups count too.

```
pb_pages/
  +middleware.js         # runs first (all routes)
  products/
    +middleware.js       # runs second (/products/...)
    [id]/
      +middleware.js     # runs third (/products/[id])
```

The full order for a request is:

1. Plugins' `onRequest`
2. Middleware, root first
3. The folder's `+page.js` or `+api.js` (`load`, then the method's handler)
4. The template, then layouts, innermost first
5. The response

If any step sends a response, the later steps are skipped.

## Common uses

### Auth guard

```js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
  return next()
}
```

### Request validation

```js
// pb_pages/products/[id]/+middleware.js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!/^[a-z0-9]+$/.test(ctx.params.id)) throw ctx.httpError(400, 'Invalid ID')
  return next()
}
```

### Shared data

```js
// pb_pages/+middleware.js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.data.categories = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('categories', 'active = true', 'name', 100)
  return next()
}
```

```ejs
<nav>
  <% for (const c of data.categories) { %>
    <a href="/categories/<%= c.id %>"><%= c.getString('name') %></a>
  <% } %>
</nav>
```

### Headers

```js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.res.header('X-Frame-Options', 'DENY')
  return next()
}
```


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/asset-management

# Asset Management

Static files in `pb_pages` (images, CSS, JS, fonts) can be served with fingerprinted URLs that change when the file changes.

## Where to put assets

Anywhere in `pb_pages`, next to the pages that use them or in a shared folder:

```
pb_pages/
  assets/
    app.css
    logo.png
  feature/
    index.md
    header.jpg
```

## In templates

Use `asset()` (the same as `ctx.asset()`):

```ejs
<link rel="stylesheet" href="<%= asset('/assets/app.css') %>">
<img src="<%= asset('header.jpg') %>">
```

`asset('/assets/app.css')` returns something like `/assets/app.3f9a1c2b7d4e.css`.

- Relative paths resolve from the current file's folder; `/`-paths from `pb_pages`.
- A path that isn't a file in `pb_pages` is returned unchanged.

## In Markdown

Relative image paths go through `asset()` automatically:

```markdown
![Header](header.jpg)
```

## How it works

1. A fingerprinted name carries the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256: `name.<hash>.ext`.
2. Fingerprinted URLs are served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
3. When the file changes, its hash and URL change, so browsers and CDNs fetch the new one.

See [asset](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/asset) and [Caching](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/caching).


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/static-content

# Serving Static Content in PocketPages

Any file in `pb_pages` that isn't a page (`.ejs`, `.md`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`), a framework file (`+...`), private (`_...`) or ignored (names starting with `-` or `.`) is a static file. It's served as-is at its path, with groups removed:

```
pb_pages/
  assets/
    app.css            -> /assets/app.css
    logo.png           -> /assets/logo.png
  documents/
    terms.pdf          -> /documents/terms.pdf
  (marketing)/
    brochure.pdf       -> /brochure.pdf
  favicon.ico          -> /favicon.ico
  index.ejs            -> /  (a page, not static)
```

- The content type comes from the extension.
- The `ETag` comes from the content hash; a matching `If-None-Match` gets `304`.
- A static file and a page can't claim the same URL (startup error).

For cache-friendly URLs, reference files through [`asset()`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/asset-management).

## `pb_pages` and `pb_public`

A URL nothing in `pb_pages` matches goes on to `pb_public`, so you can keep using `pb_public` for files you don't want next to your pages.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/secrets

# Managing Secrets in PocketPages

Keep API keys, passwords and other secrets in environment variables, and read them with `ctx.env(name)`. It returns `''` when the variable is unset.

```js
// pb_pages/checkout/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const key = ctx.env('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY')
    if (!key) throw new Error('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not set')
    // ...
  },
}
```

`ctx.env` reads the app's environment. Under a multitenant host's sandbox, it reads the instance's environment.

## Best practices

1. **Never put secrets in the page.** Anything a template outputs goes to the browser.

   ```ejs
   <!-- DON'T -->
   <meta name="api-key" content="<%= ctx.env('API_KEY') %>">

   <!-- OK: a public value -->
   <meta name="api-endpoint" content="<%= ctx.env('PUBLIC_API_ENDPOINT') %>">
   ```

2. **Check for required variables** and fail clearly when one is missing.
3. **Use descriptive names**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, not `KEY`.
4. **Never commit secrets** to version control, and use different values in development and production.

## Setting environment variables

```bash
# Shell
export STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_...
pocketone serve
```

```dockerfile
# Docker
ENV STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_...
```


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/config

# Configuration with `+config.js`

Create `pb_pages/+config.js` to configure PocketPages for the app. It's only allowed at the top of `pb_pages`; a `+config.js` in a subfolder is an error at startup.

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'],
  debug: false,
}
```

## Options

| Key | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `plugins` | `[]` | Built-in plugins by name, or JS plugin factories. EJS and Markdown are always on. |
| `debug` | `false` | Detailed error pages and `ctx.log.debug` output even outside dev mode. |

`+config.js` must export an object; exporting a function (0.x's `(api) => ({...})` form) is an error.

`+config.js` runs on each page request, so these aren't caught at startup: unknown keys, names that are neither a
module nor a built-in, or a plugin listed twice make every page answer with an error (a 500; dev mode shows the
reason on the page), and the reason goes to the log.

## Plugins

Each entry in `plugins` is one of:

- **A name**, loaded with `require`: a `_private/` file (`'datastar'` for the [Datastar add-on](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/datastar)),
  then a package in `node_modules`, then a built-in (`'auth'` or `'realtime'`). It must export a plugin factory. See
  [Plugins](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins).
- **A JS plugin factory**: a function that returns hooks, such as `require('./_private/my-plugin.js')`. A `require`
  with a path loads exactly that file, skipping the name lookup, so it's how you choose one copy over another.
- **An object with a factory and options**: `{ factory, ...options }`. The object is passed to the factory as its `config`.

```js
module.exports = {
  plugins: [
    'auth',
    'realtime',
    { factory: require('./_private/banner.js'), text: 'Hello' },
  ],
}
```

Plugin hooks run in the order the plugins are listed. See [Plugin Authoring](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/authoring).

## Debug

`debug: true` turns on what dev mode (`--dev`) turns on: detailed error pages and `ctx.log.debug` output. See [Debugging](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/debugging).


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/caching

# Understanding Caching in PocketPages

## Fingerprinted assets

`asset()` adds a content hash to a file's URL:

```ejs
<img src="<%= asset('/images/logo.png') %>">
<!-- <img src="/images/logo.3f9a1c2b7d4e.png"> -->
```

- The hash is the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256.
- Fingerprinted URLs are served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, so browsers and CDNs keep them for a year.
- When the file changes, the hash changes, and so does the URL. Old copies are never served for the new URL.
- A path that isn't a file in `pb_pages` is returned unchanged (and not fingerprinted).

## Static files

Every static file gets an `ETag` from its content hash. A request with a matching `If-None-Match` gets `304 Not Modified`.

## Templates

A template is compiled once per content hash and reused. Edit a file and the next request uses the new version, in every mode.

## Routes

The route table is built at startup and rebuilt whenever anything in `pb_pages` changes. A rebuild never restarts the app.

## Pages

Rendered pages aren't cached. To let browsers or a CDN cache a page, set a header in a handler or middleware:

```js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.res.header('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=60')
  return next()
}
```


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/errors

# Errors

## Thrown errors

Anything thrown in middleware, a handler or a template becomes a `500`.

- **Dev mode or `debug: true`:** an HTML error page with the message, the file and line (template lines map to the `.ejs` or `.md` source), and the stack trimmed to `pb_pages`-relative paths.
- **Otherwise:** a plain "Something went wrong" page.

The full error always goes to the app's log.

## `ctx.httpError(status, message)`

Throw `ctx.httpError()` to answer with a specific status:

```js
// pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    let product
    try {
      product = ctx.app.findFirstRecordByData('products', 'slug', ctx.params.id)
    } catch (e) {
      throw ctx.httpError(404, 'No such product') // findFirstRecordByData throws when nothing matches
    }
    ctx.data.product = product
  },
}
```

- In a page, it sends that status with a plain page showing `message`.
- In a `+api.js`, it sends JSON: `{ "status": 404, "message": "No such product" }`.

## A custom error page

Create `pb_pages/+error.ejs`. It renders for every `ctx.httpError` and for every `500` outside dev mode, inside the root layout, with `ctx.error = { status, message }`:

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/+error.ejs -->
<% slot('title', () => { %>Error <%= ctx.error.status %><% }) %>
<h1><%= ctx.error.status %></h1>
<p><%= ctx.error.message %></p>
```

`+error` and `+404` live only at the top of `pb_pages`. Either may be `.ejs`, `.jsx` or `.tsx`.

## A custom 404 page

Create `pb_pages/+404.ejs`. It renders inside the root layout, with status `404`, for a `GET` or `HEAD` that nothing answers: no page, no file in `pb_public` and no PocketBase route. It never renders for `/api/` or `/_/`. The root `+middleware.js` runs first, and page code can still change the status.

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/+404.ejs -->
<% slot('title', () => { %>Not found<% }) %>
<h1>Not found</h1>
<p>Nothing lives at <%= ctx.req.url.pathname %>.</p>
```


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/debugging

# Debugging in PocketPages

## Dev mode

Run `pocketone` with `--dev`:

```bash
pocketone serve --dev
```

Dev mode turns on:

- detailed error pages (message, file and line, trimmed stack; see [Errors](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/errors));
- `ctx.log.debug` output.

## `debug: true`

To get the same in production, set `debug: true` in `+config.js`:

```js
module.exports = {
  debug: true,
}
```

Turn it off again when you're done. Detailed error pages show error messages, file paths and stack traces to anyone who triggers an error.

## Logging

`ctx.log` writes to the app's log:

```js
ctx.log.debug('loaded product', ctx.params.id)  // only in dev mode or with debug: true
ctx.log.info('order placed')
ctx.log.warn('stock is low')
ctx.log.error('payment failed')
```

See [log](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/log).

## Template changes

Templates are cached by content hash and the route table is rebuilt on any file change, in every mode. If a change doesn't show, check the app's log for a startup error (bad file name, route conflict): the previous route table keeps serving until the error is fixed.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/deploying

# Going Live

A PocketPages app is a `pb_pages` folder. To go live, run PocketOne on your server (pages is built in) and put `pb_pages` next to `pb_data`, along with your other `pb_*` folders:

```
pb_data/
pb_hooks/
pb_migrations/
pb_public/
pb_pages/
```

Or point `pocketone` at it with `--pagesDir`.

## Updating

Copy the changed files into `pb_pages`. The route table is rebuilt on any change, and templates are cached by content hash, so updates show on the next request without restarting the app. If an update has a startup error (a bad name or a route conflict), it's logged with the file path and the previous route table keeps serving.

## Before you go live

- Run without `--dev`, and keep `debug: false` in `+config.js`.
- Set secrets as environment variables (see [Managing Secrets](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/secrets)).
- Serve over HTTPS. Cookies set with `ctx.res.cookie` are marked `Secure` on HTTPS requests.

## Multitenant hosts

Under a multitenant PocketOne host, every instance has its own `pb_pages`, and page code runs with the same limits as the rest of the instance's JS.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins

# Plugins

Plugins add features to `ctx` and hook into each request. Turn them on in `+config.js`:

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'],
}
```

Each entry is one of:

- **A name in quotes.** It's loaded with `require`, which looks in this order:
  1. a `_private/` folder in `pb_pages` (`'datastar'` finds `_private/datastar.js`)
  2. `pb_pages/node_modules`, for a package from your `package.json`
  3. the built-in plugins, `'auth'` and `'realtime'`

  A path such as `'./plugins/my-plugin.js'` works too.
- **A plugin factory**, usually `require('./_private/my-plugin.js')`. Writing the `require` yourself with a path skips
  the lookup above and loads exactly that file, which is how you pick one copy over another: `'datastar'` would find
  `_private/datastar.js` first, while `require('./node_modules/datastar')` always loads the package.

Datastar isn't built in. It's an add-on file you copy into `pb_pages/_private/` and list by name.

EJS and Markdown are always on; they aren't plugins.

## Built-in plugins

| Name | Adds |
|---|---|
| [`auth`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/auth) | Cookie sessions on PocketBase auth: sets `ctx.auth` from the `pb_auth` cookie and adds `ctx.session.*` sign-in methods. |
| [`realtime`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/realtime) | `ctx.realtime.send()` to PocketBase realtime subscribers. |

## JS plugins

A JS plugin is a module that exports a factory returning hooks. List it by name, or `require()` it yourself, which you
need for options (`{ factory, ...options }`):

```js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth', 'my-plugin', { factory: require('./_private/other-plugin.js'), color: 'blue' }],
}
```

See [Plugin Authoring](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/authoring).

| Add-on | Adds |
|---|---|
| [Datastar](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/datastar) | `ctx.datastar.*` helpers for [Datastar](https://data-star.dev). Copy [`addons/datastar.js`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/addons/datastar.js) into `pb_pages/_private/`; the `datastar` starter kit already has it. |

## Order

Plugins' hooks run in the order they're listed, and `onRequest` hooks run before any middleware.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/auth

# Authentication Plugin

The `auth` plugin gives you cookie sessions on PocketBase auth. It calls the app directly, not over HTTP.

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth'],
}
```

## What it does on every request

It reads the `pb_auth` cookie, validates the token and sets `ctx.auth` to the authenticated record. A bad cookie is cleared.

`ctx.auth` is also set without the plugin when a request carries PocketBase's own `Authorization` header.

## `ctx.session`

| Method | |
|---|---|
| `register(email, password, { collection = 'users', data, verify = true, signIn = true }?)` | Create an auth record. `data` holds extra fields. `verify` sends the verification email; `signIn` signs the new account in (returns `{ token: '', record }` when `false`). |
| `signInWithPassword(email, password, { collection }?)` | Sign in with a password. |
| `requestOTP(email, { collection, create = false }?)` | Send a one-time password. Returns the `otpId`. An unknown email still gets an id, one that never validates; with `create: true` the account is created first. |
| `signInWithOTP(otpId, code, { collection }?)` | Sign in with a one-time password. |
| `signInAnonymously({ collection }?)` | Sign in as a new anonymous user. |
| `requestOAuth2(provider, { collection, redirectPath = '/auth/oauth/confirm', redirect = true }?)` | Store state in a cookie and return the provider's URL. With `redirect` it also sends the redirect; pass `redirect: false` to send the URL some other way. `redirectPath` must be a path on this site. |
| `signInWithOAuth2(state, code, { createData }?)` | Complete an OAuth2 sign-in on the redirect path. Returns `{ token, record, meta }`; `meta.isNew` is `true` for a new account. |
| `signIn(record)` | Set the cookie for a record you authenticated yourself. It skips the MFA check below. |
| `signOut()` | Sign out. |
| `authMethods({ collection }?)` | The sign-in methods a collection has turned on: `{ password: { enabled, identityFields }, otp: { enabled }, mfa: { enabled }, oauth2: { enabled, providers: [{ name, displayName }] } }`, as PocketBase's auth-methods API. |

### MFA

Pages doesn't have a second sign-in step yet. If a collection has MFA turned on (Collections → `users` → Options →
Multi-factor authentication) and its MFA rule matches the account, every sign-in method above refuses it with "This
account needs a second sign-in step (MFA), which pages doesn't support yet." An empty rule matches every account. To
use pages sign-in, turn MFA off for the collection, or give it a rule that leaves out the accounts that sign in here.

Every sign-in method sets `ctx.auth` for the rest of the request and returns `{ token, record }`.

### Email flows

These use PocketBase's own checks and mail templates. The request methods never reveal whether an email exists.

| Method | |
|---|---|
| `requestVerification(email, { collection }?)` | Send the verification email (skipped for an account that's already verified). |
| `confirmVerification(token)` | Mark the account verified. Returns the record. |
| `requestPasswordReset(email, { collection }?)` | Send the password reset email. |
| `confirmPasswordReset(token, password, passwordConfirm)` | Set the new password (and mark the account verified). Returns the record. |
| `requestEmailChange(newEmail)` | Send a confirmation email to `newEmail`. Needs a signed-in user (`ctx.auth`). |
| `confirmEmailChange(token, password)` | Change the email after checking the current password. Returns the record. |

A bad or expired token throws an error.

## Example

```js
// pb_pages/login/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { email, password } = ctx.req.body()
    try {
      ctx.session.signInWithPassword(email, password)
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: 'Invalid email or password', email }
    }
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

```js
// pb_pages/logout/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.signOut()
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

See the [Authentication guide](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/authentication) for complete flows: registration, one-time passwords, OAuth2 and anonymous sign-in.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/datastar

# Datastar Add-on

The Datastar add-on adds helpers for [Datastar](https://data-star.dev). It's a JS plugin that ships with PocketPages
rather than a built-in: copy [`addons/datastar.js`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/addons/datastar.js)
into `pb_pages/_private/` (the `datastar` starter kit already has it) and list it in `+config.js` by name:

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['datastar'],
}
```

Add the script tags to your root layout's `<head>`. They load [Datastar](https://data-star.dev) v1.0.5. Datastar 1.0 uses
a colon between the attribute name and its key (`data-on:click`, `data-bind:name`, `data-signals:count`,
`data-class:active`, `data-attr:href`); the older hyphen form (`data-on-click`) is ignored. See the
[Datastar attribute reference](https://data-star.dev/reference/attributes).

```ejs
<head>
  <%- ctx.datastar.scripts() %>
</head>
```

## `ctx.datastar`

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `scripts({ spa, realtime }?)` | Returns the script tags. |
| `patchElements(html, { selector, mode, useViewTransition, viewTransitionSelector, namespace }?)` | Sends a patch-elements SSE event on the current response. `mode` is `outer` (default), `inner`, `replace`, `prepend`, `append`, `before`, `after` or `remove`; `namespace` is `html` (default), `svg` or `mathml`. |
| `patchSignals(signals, { onlyIfMissing }?)` | Sends a patch-signals SSE event (JSON Merge Patch: `null` removes a signal). |
| `executeScript(js, { autoRemove, attributes }?)` | Sends a script to run in the browser. |
| `consoleLog(msg)` / `consoleError(err)` | Logs to the browser console. |
| `redirect(url)` | Sends the browser to `url` (a full page load). A Datastar fetch can't follow `ctx.res.redirect`, so use this from `@get`/`@post` handlers. |
| `dispatchCustomEvent(name, detail, { selector }?)` | Fires a `CustomEvent` on `document`, or on the elements matching `selector`. |
| `replaceURL(url)` | Changes the address bar without a navigation (`history.replaceState`). |
| `prefetch(urls)` | Adds speculation rules so the browser prefetches `urls`. |
| `signals()` | Reads the request's signals as an object: from the `datastar` query parameter for GET and DELETE, from the body otherwise. |
| `readSignals(target)` | Merges the request's signals into `target` and returns it (0.x's `readSignals(request, target)` also works). |
| `realtime.*` | Sends the same patches to realtime subscribers. Needs the [`realtime`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/realtime) plugin. |

Every send also takes `eventId` and `retryDuration` (in ms; the default 1000 isn't sent).

## Pages as patches

When a request has the `Datastar-Request: true` header, the rendered page is sent without layouts, as a `patchElements` event. If the request has a `Datastar-Selector` header, the patch goes into that element.

This is how this site navigates between docs pages: the layout calls

```ejs
<%- ctx.datastar.scripts({ spa: { scope: '#toc', selector: '#content' } }) %>
```

so links in the table of contents fetch the page and patch it into `#content`. Plain left-clicks are intercepted;
modified clicks (Cmd/Ctrl/Shift/Alt, middle-click), links with a `target` attribute and links to other origins navigate
normally. Back/Forward work, including back to the page you landed on: each page opens at the top, and Back/Forward
return you to where you were scrolled.

## Example: a counter

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/counter/index.ejs -->
<button data-on:click="@post('/counter')">
  Count: <span id="count"><%= ctx.store('count') || 0 %></span>
</button>
```

```js
// pb_pages/counter/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const count = (ctx.store('count') || 0) + 1
    ctx.store('count', count)
    ctx.datastar.patchElements(`<span id="count">${count}</span>`)
  },
}
```

## Example: reading signals

```js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { name, email } = ctx.datastar.signals()
    if (!name || !email) {
      ctx.datastar.patchSignals({ error: 'Please fill all fields' })
      return
    }
    ctx.datastar.patchElements('<div id="form">Thanks!</div>')
  },
}
```

## Broadcasting

With the `realtime` plugin on, `ctx.datastar.realtime.*` sends patches to every realtime subscriber instead of the current response:

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = { plugins: ['realtime', 'datastar'] }
```

```js
ctx.datastar.realtime.patchElements(`<span id="count">${count}</span>`)
```


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/realtime

# Realtime Plugin

The `realtime` plugin sends messages to [PocketBase realtime](https://pocketbase.io/docs/realtime/) subscribers.

```js
// pb_pages/+config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['realtime'],
}
```

## `ctx.realtime.send(topic, data, { filter }?)`

Sends `data` to the subscribers of `topic`. `filter(client)` may limit the recipients.

```js
// pb_pages/ping/+api.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.realtime.send('ping', { at: new Date().toISOString() })
    return ctx.res.json({ ok: true })
  },
}
```

On the client, subscribe with the PocketBase JS SDK:

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/pocketbase/dist/pocketbase.umd.js"></script>
<script>
  const pb = new PocketBase(location.origin)
  pb.realtime.subscribe('ping', (data) => console.log('Received:', data))
</script>
```

## Filtering recipients

```js
ctx.realtime.send('alerts', 'Maintenance at 10:00', {
  filter: (client) => !!client.get('auth'),
})
```

## Sending HTML

For hypermedia libraries (HTMX, Datastar), send rendered HTML. `include()` is available in templates, so render the partial there:

```js
// pb_pages/xapi/chat/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post() {}, // accept POST; the page renders and sends
}
```

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/xapi/chat/index.ejs -->
<% ctx.realtime.send('chat', include('chat-msg', { message: ctx.req.body().message })) %>
```

See [Realtime Events](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/realtime) and the [Datastar add-on](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/datastar), which can send Datastar patches over realtime.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/authoring

# Plugin Authoring Guide

A JS plugin is a factory that returns hooks:

```js
// pb_pages/_private/my-plugin.js
module.exports = (config) => ({
  name: 'my-plugin',
  onRequest(ctx) {},                                   // before middleware
  extendContext(ctx) { ctx.hello = () => 'hi' },
  transform({ html, ctx, file }) { return html },      // after each template or layout renders
})
```

Turn it on in `+config.js`:

```js
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['my-plugin'], // pb_pages/_private/my-plugin.js
}
```

## `config`

`config` is the plugin's entry in `+config.js` when that entry is an object (`{ factory, ...options }`), else `{}`:

```js
module.exports = {
  plugins: [{ factory: require('./_private/banner.js'), text: 'Beta' }],
}
```

```js
// pb_pages/_private/banner.js
module.exports = (config) => ({
  name: 'banner',
  transform({ html }) {
    return html.replace('<body>', `<body><div class="banner">${config.text}</div>`)
  },
})
```

## Hooks

Every hook is optional. Hooks run in the order plugins are listed in `+config.js`.

| Hook | When |
|---|---|
| `name` | The plugin's name. |
| `onRequest(ctx)` | At the start of each request, before middleware. |
| `extendContext(ctx)` | Add members to `ctx`. |
| `transform({ html, ctx, file })` | After each template or layout renders. Return the new HTML. |

## Example: a context helper

```js
module.exports = () => ({
  name: 'format',
  extendContext(ctx) {
    ctx.formatDate = (d) => new Date(d).toLocaleDateString()
  },
})
```

```ejs
<p>Posted <%= ctx.formatDate(data.post.getString('created')) %></p>
```

## Permissions

JS plugins run with the same permissions as the rest of the app's JS. Under a multitenant host, that means the instance's sandbox.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx

# The `ctx` Object

PocketPages creates one `ctx` object per request and passes it to middleware, handlers, templates and plugins.

```js
// +middleware.js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => next()

// +page.js / +api.js
module.exports = { load(ctx) {} }
```

```ejs
<!-- any template -->
<p><%= ctx.req.url.pathname %></p>
```

In templates, `data`, `params`, `asset` and `meta` are shortcuts for `ctx.data`, `ctx.params`, `ctx.asset` and `ctx.meta`.

## Members

| Member | |
|---|---|
| [`ctx.req`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/req) | The request: method, URL, query, headers, cookies, body, files |
| [`ctx.res`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/res) | The response: status, headers, cookies, redirects, JSON, HTML, text, files, SSE |
| [`ctx.data`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/data) | Plain object shared by middleware, handlers and templates |
| [`ctx.params`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/data#ctxparams) | Route parameters |
| [`ctx.route`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/data#ctxroute) | The matched route: `{ path, name, file }` |
| [`ctx.flash()`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/flash) | The one-time message from the previous redirect |
| [`ctx.auth`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/auth) | The authenticated record, or `null` |
| [`ctx.app`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/app) | The app (`$app`) |
| [`ctx.pb()`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/pb) | A JS SDK client acting as the visitor (API rules apply) |
| [`ctx.env(name)`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/env) | Environment variable |
| [`ctx.log`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/log) | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` |
| [`ctx.meta(key, value?)`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/meta) | Per-request page metadata |
| [`ctx.asset(path)`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/asset) | Fingerprinted URL for a static file |
| [`ctx.include(name, locals?)`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/partials) | Render a `_private/` partial from JS and get its text (same lookup as `include`, from the route's folder) |
| [`ctx.resolve(name, { mode }?)`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/resolve) | Load a module from `_private/` |
| [`ctx.store(name, value?)`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/store) | The app's in-memory store |
| `ctx.pagesDir` | Absolute path of the app's `pb_pages` folder (read-only), e.g. for `$os.readDir` |
| `ctx.dev` | `true` in dev mode |
| [`ctx.httpError(status, message)`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/errors) | An error to throw for a specific status |
| [`ctx.error`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/errors) | `{ status, message }`, in `+error.ejs` |

## Added by plugins

| Member | Plugin |
|---|---|
| `ctx.session` | [auth](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/auth) |
| `ctx.realtime` | [realtime](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/realtime) |
| `ctx.datastar` | [datastar](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/datastar) |

JS plugins can add their own members with [`extendContext`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/authoring).


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/req

# `ctx.req`

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `method` | `"GET"`, `"POST"`, ... |
| `url` | `{ href, origin, pathname, search }` |
| `query(name)` | First value of a query parameter as a string, or `undefined` |
| `query(name, { all: true })` | Every value, as an array of strings |
| `query()` | `{ name: firstValue }` for every parameter |
| `header(name)` | Request header, `''` if absent |
| `cookie(name)` | Cookie value as a string, or `undefined` |
| `cookie(name, { json: true })` | Cookie parsed as JSON (`undefined` if absent or not JSON) |
| `cookies()` | `{ name: value }`, strings |
| `body()` | Parsed body: a JSON object, or form fields as `{ name: value }` (repeated names as arrays) |
| `files(name)` | Uploaded files for a multipart field, as PocketBase `*filesystem.File` values ready for a record field |
| `ip` | Client IP as PocketBase resolves it (trusted proxy settings apply) |
| `event` | The underlying PocketBase `RequestEvent`, for anything not covered here |

Query values and cookies are strings unless you ask for JSON. Nothing is parsed for you.

## Examples

```ejs
<p>You asked for <%= ctx.req.url.pathname %><%= ctx.req.url.search %></p>
<p>Page <%= Number(ctx.req.query('page') ?? 1) %></p>
<p>Browser: <%= ctx.req.header('User-Agent') %></p>
```

### Forms

`body()` parses JSON, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and `multipart/form-data`:

```js
// pb_pages/contact/+page.js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { email, message } = ctx.req.body()
    // ...
  },
}
```

### File uploads

```html
<form method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
  <input type="file" name="avatar" />
  <button>Upload</button>
</form>
```

```js
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const record = ctx.app.findRecordById('users', ctx.auth.id)
    record.set('avatar', ctx.req.files('avatar')[0])
    ctx.app.save(record)
    return ctx.res.redirect('/account')
  },
}
```

### Cookies

```js
const theme = ctx.req.cookie('theme')                     // 'dark' or undefined
const prefs = ctx.req.cookie('prefs', { json: true }) ?? {}
```

Set cookies with [`ctx.res.cookie()`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/res#cookies).


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/res

# `ctx.res`

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `status(code)` | Status for the rendered page. Returns `ctx.res`. |
| `header(name, value)` | Set a response header. `header(name)` reads it back. |
| `cookie(name, value, options?)` | Set a cookie. |
| `clearCookie(name, options?)` | Expire a cookie (same `path` / `domain` as when set). |
| `redirect(location, { status = 302, flash }?)` or `redirect(location, status)` | Send a redirect. `status` must be a 3xx code. `flash` sets a [one-time message](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/flash). |
| `json(data)` / `json(status, data)` | Send JSON. |
| `html(html)` / `html(status, html)` | Send HTML as-is (no layouts). |
| `text(text)` / `text(status, text)` | Send plain text. |
| `file(path)` | Send a file from `pb_pages` (path relative to `pb_pages`). |
| `sse()` | Start a `text/event-stream` response. |
| `layout(false)` | Render this page without layouts (e.g. an HTML fragment for htmx). Returns `ctx.res`. |
| `sent` | `true` once a response has been sent. |

Once a response is sent, the later steps of the request (handlers, template, layouts) are skipped.

## Status and headers

```ejs
<% ctx.res.status(404).header('Cache-Control', 'no-store') %>
<h1>Not here</h1>
```

## Redirects

```js
return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
return ctx.res.redirect('/account', { flash: 'Saved' })
return ctx.res.redirect('/new-home', 301) // or { status: 301 }
```

## Cookies

```js
ctx.res.cookie('theme', 'dark', { maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24 * 365 })
ctx.res.cookie('prefs', { compact: true })   // objects are JSON.stringify'd
ctx.res.clearCookie('theme')
```

- Non-string values are `JSON.stringify`'d. The value is then percent-encoded (`encodeURIComponent`), and `ctx.req.cookie` decodes it.
- Defaults: `path=/`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, and `Secure` when the request is HTTPS.
- Options: `path`, `domain`, `maxAge` (seconds), `expires` (a `Date`, milliseconds since the epoch, or a date string; with `maxAge` too, browsers use `maxAge`), `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite`.

## JSON, HTML, text and files

```js
return ctx.res.json({ ok: true })
return ctx.res.json(201, { id: record.id })
return ctx.res.html('<p>Fragment</p>')
return ctx.res.text(404, 'Not found')
return ctx.res.file('downloads/manual.pdf')
```

## Server-sent events

`sse()` starts a `text/event-stream` response and returns `{ send(event, data, { id, retry }?), comment(text), close() }`:

```js
// pb_pages/clock/+api.js
module.exports = {
  get(ctx) {
    const stream = ctx.res.sse()
    stream.send('time', new Date().toISOString())
    stream.close()
  },
}
```

Streaming is only available through `sse()`. Templates return their text all at once.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/data

# `ctx.data`, `ctx.params`, `ctx.route`

## `ctx.data`

A plain object shared by middleware, handlers and templates. It starts as `{}`. In templates it's also available as `data`.

```js
// +middleware.js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.data.user = ctx.auth
  return next()
}
```

```js
// +page.js
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    return { products: ctx.app.findAllRecords('products') }  // Object.assign'd into ctx.data
  },
}
```

```ejs
<% for (const p of data.products) { %>
  <li><%= p.getString('name') %></li>
<% } %>
```

A handler's returned object is shallow-assigned into `ctx.data`. There is no deep merge.

## `ctx.params`

Route parameters from `[name]` segments, as strings. Never includes query parameters (use [`ctx.req.query()`](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/req)). In templates it's also available as `params`.

```ejs
<!-- pb_pages/[org]/[repo]/index.ejs, at /acme/web -->
<p><%= params.org %>/<%= params.repo %></p>  <!-- acme/web -->
```

## `ctx.route`

`{ path, name, file }`: the route pattern, the page name and its file relative to `pb_pages`.

| Page file | `path` | `name` |
|---|---|---|
| `products/[id].ejs` | `/products/[id]` | `[id]` |
| `docs/index.md` | `/docs` | `index` |

A `+page.js` applies to every page in its folder; use `ctx.route.name` to tell them apart.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/flash

# `ctx.flash()`

A flash is a one-time message that survives one redirect, such as "Saved" after a form post.

## Setting a flash

```js
return ctx.res.redirect('/account', { flash: 'Saved' })
```

The message is stored as JSON in a cookie (`pp_flash`, `HttpOnly`, `Max-Age=300`). It can be any JSON value:

```js
return ctx.res.redirect('/cart', { flash: { type: 'success', text: 'Added to cart' } })
```

## Reading it

On the next request, `ctx.flash()` returns the message and clears the cookie. It returns `undefined` when there is none. Calling it again in the same request returns the same value.

```ejs
<% const flash = ctx.flash() %>
<% if (flash) { %>
  <div class="alert alert-<%= flash.type %>"><%= flash.text %></div>
<% } %>
```

Read it in your layout to show flashes on every page.


---

Source: https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/auth

# `ctx.auth`

The authenticated record, or `null`. It's set by:

- PocketBase's own auth, when the request has an `Authorization` header;
- the [`auth` plugin](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/auth), from its `pb_auth` cookie.

```ejs
<% if (ctx.auth) { %>
  <p>Welcome, <%= ctx.auth.email() %></p>
  <% if (!ctx.auth.verified()) { %><p>Please verify your email.</p><% } %>
<% } else { %>
  <a href="/login">Log in</a>
<% } %>
```
